items.title: Finite type points are exactly the points through which the residual gerbe includes as a morphism of finite type
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project — Morphisms of Algebraic Stacks

items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement characterises finite type points of an algebraic stack as those for which the residual gerbe exists and includes into the stack by a morphism locally of finite type, with an intermediate condition through a singleton stack mapping to the stack (author lemma at source lines 3802-3816, label lemma-point-finite-type-monomorphism). The proof (source lines 3818-3910) builds from a smooth presentation of the point the groupoid presentation of that point, checks that its structure maps are locally of finite type and, over a field, flat and locally of finite presentation, obtains the quotient stack, identifies it with the residual gerbe by the uniqueness statement, and then transfers local finiteness of the inclusion from a base change along an fppf covering by the descent statement; the remaining implications close the circle using the identification of finite type points through morphisms (proof lines 3824-3909). The construction of the residual gerbe from the groupoid presentation is the content. H3.
